title: Final assessment part 1: Framework fundamentals and HTTP

questions.prompt: What is the role of a Flask view function?
options: Flask includes a built-in full ORM and authentication server by default.
Flask provides a WSGI web application framework that can be extended with separately selected packages.
Flask is a browser-side JavaScript framework.
Flask requires every application to use a particular SQL database.
questions.answer_key: Flask provides a WSGI application framework and leaves many integrations to separately chosen packages.
questions.explanation: This question checks flask core and extension responsibilities. Confirm the relevant behavior in the official Flask documentation and test the failure boundary rather than relying on assumptions.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between a route endpoint and a URL?
options: 200 with an unrelated success payload
302 to an arbitrary external destination
404 Not Found with a safe response body
500 with a stack trace sent to the client
questions.answer_key: 404 Not Found with a safe response body
questions.explanation: This question checks http errors. Confirm the relevant behavior in the official Flask documentation and test the failure boundary rather than relying on assumptions.

questions.prompt: How should an unsupported HTTP method be handled?
options: Only in client-side JavaScript
Only in a template
At the server boundary before applying the operation
Only after a database error happens
questions.answer_key: At the server boundary before applying the operation
questions.explanation: This question checks server-side validation. Confirm the relevant behavior in the official Flask documentation and test the failure boundary rather than relying on assumptions.

questions.prompt: Which practice helps prevent SQL injection?
options: Construct SQL by concatenating request strings
Use parameterized queries or supported ORM expressions
Hide the query from the browser
Store request values in a session cookie
questions.answer_key: Use parameterized queries or supported ORM expressions
questions.explanation: This question checks database security. Confirm the relevant behavior in the official Flask documentation and test the failure boundary rather than relying on assumptions.

options: A database backup
A modular group of routes and related application behavior that is registered on an app
Automatic encryption of every database field
An isolated process for executing untrusted code
questions.answer_key: A modular group of routes and related application behavior that is registered on an app
questions.explanation: This question checks modular architecture. Confirm the relevant behavior in the official Flask documentation and test the failure boundary rather than relying on assumptions.

questions.prompt: Which is appropriate for production request handling?
options: Use the interactive development debugger publicly
Disable all logs
Use a production WSGI server and reviewed environment settings
Store the secret key in a public repository
questions.answer_key: Use a production WSGI server and reviewed environment settings
questions.explanation: This question checks deployment. Confirm the relevant behavior in the official Flask documentation and test the failure boundary rather than relying on assumptions.

questions.prompt: What should a test for a protected route assert?
options: Only that the template file exists
Both allowed access and denial for an unauthenticated or unauthorized request
Only the color of a button
That it always returns 200 regardless of identity
questions.answer_key: Both allowed access and denial for an unauthenticated or unauthorized request
questions.explanation: This question checks authentication and authorization tests. Confirm the relevant behavior in the official Flask documentation and test the failure boundary rather than relying on assumptions.

questions.prompt: Which best describes Flask default sessions?
options: An encrypted server-side database by default
A signed cookie-based mechanism, so sensitive secrets should not be stored there
A replacement for authorization
A mechanism that makes cookies impossible to replay
questions.answer_key: A signed cookie-based mechanism, so sensitive secrets should not be stored there
questions.explanation: This question checks sessions. Confirm the relevant behavior in the official Flask documentation and test the failure boundary rather than relying on assumptions.

questions.prompt: What does HTTP CORS configuration do?
options: Authenticate every request by itself
Control which browser origins are permitted to read certain cross-origin responses; it is not authentication
Encrypt the connection without TLS
Replace CSRF defenses
questions.answer_key: Control which browser origins are permitted to read certain cross-origin responses; it is not authentication
questions.explanation: This question checks cors and security. Confirm the relevant behavior in the official Flask documentation and test the failure boundary rather than relying on assumptions.

questions.prompt: What is a safe way to approach performance improvement?
options: Change many settings without measurement
Use one short unrepeatable measurement
Measure a representative baseline, identify the bottleneck, change one factor, and compare
Disable all validation to speed things up
questions.answer_key: Measure a representative baseline, identify the bottleneck, change one factor, and compare
questions.explanation: This question checks performance. Confirm the relevant behavior in the official Flask documentation and test the failure boundary rather than relying on assumptions.
